A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR10 and SVHN experiments, method comparisons, ablations and capacity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Imagenette experiments, masking and capacity checks, a redirection trajectory and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, step 2.2, changes the removal objective from L_step2 = L_remove to L_step2 = -L_remove. This corrects the specified loss sign; the expansion, NPO removal, masking, repair and final partition removal remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: v2 adds Imagenette evaluation in Appendix A.7 and Tables 6–7. CIFAR10 and SVHN remain, with the same random-label, inter-class confusion and poison-trigger tasks. This is a limited extension of image-classification coverage.

E2.justification: Retained comparisons preserve their comparator membership, and added experiments reuse previously evaluated methods. NPO was already evaluated in v1; its expanded description in v2 does not introduce a new baseline. Added full-capacity ViT rows concern configurations of existing comparators.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation settings with 5%-active masks, Imagenette runs using 100 corruptions and 50%/90% capacity configurations, full-capacity ViT references, a five-epoch redirection trace and relative-runtime measurements. Section 6 also changes the stated healing population from Df to Dc. The retained scores and appendix descriptions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct examination of corruption redirection over unlearning epochs (Figure 5), seed sensitivity evidence (A.3), smaller-mask experiments (Tables 8–9), ViT capacity checks (Table 5) and computational profiling (A.8). These substantially broaden validation beyond the retained component ablations and earlier capacity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 0, 1 and 2 and report ±1 SEM. v2 additionally explains that the global seed affects masks and reports individual healing and utility outcomes for those seeds in a representative experiment. No increased run count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 4 and the matched detailed heatmaps retain their numerical results. Substantial new results appear in Tables 6–9, two full-capacity ViT rows, the redirection trace, seed outcomes and runtime measurements. For example, Imagenette Table 6 reports Utility×Healed of 60.98±2.02 for REM versus 54.52±2.89 for SCRUB; these are new-setting results, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the mathematical definition of the step-2 objective by adding a minus sign, a non-equivalent change. The C-score definition in Equation 1, combined loss in Equation 2 and formal problem assumptions remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the discovery-rate/regularity taxonomy, predictable limitations of prior methods, and REM's strong performance across that task space. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of why pretrained generalizable knowledge should remain in the original partition, discusses possible transformer/LLM applicability, and interprets runtime and memory tradeoffs. It also attributes narrower Imagenette gaps to fewer corruptions. Existing limitations concerning retain-set access, masking and the removal method are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link and reproducibility statement, explains REM expansion placement in ViT and global mask seeding, and documents Imagenette settings and computational costs. v1 already provided the main hyperparameter table, seeds, hardware and overall training-time estimate; those details remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same works. v2 adds explicit positioning of NPO against gradient-ascent collapse, connects the aggregate metric to Zhao et al., and uses Ghosal et al. to motivate possible scaling beyond vision. The lettered prior-work mapping preserves the earlier taxonomy assignments.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v2 expands the masking explanation, adds a reproducibility section and appendix subsections, and makes local wording, heading, citation-style and author-footnote edits. These do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with a new redirection plot and four experimental tables, enlarges Table 5, and replaces Figure 1's numerical citations with lettered regions and a mapping. Conference formatting changes typography and float placement. Earlier Figures 5–10 are retained as Figures 6–11.

improvement.justification: The redirection trace, additional benchmark and masking checks, and measured efficiency strengthen support for REM's existing empirical argument. The corrected loss sign, clearer healing population and repository link improve reproducibility. These are useful gains while the central claims and original results remain stable. The additional experiments remain within vision classification and do not establish the suggested broader scalability.
